name: Congenital Primary Megaureter, Refluxing and Obstructed Form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital primary megaureter

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of ureteral dilation with distal ureteral narrowing
Presence of vesicoureteral reflux confirmed by voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG)
Functional obstruction at the ureterovesical junction demonstrated by diuretic renography
Clinical signs such as recurrent urinary tract infections or hydronephrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ureteral dilation with distal narrowing on imaging plus confirmed vesicoureteral reflux and functional obstruction at the ureterovesical junction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes of megaureter such as neurogenic bladder or acquired obstruction.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hydroureteronephrosis detected on prenatal or postnatal ultrasound
searchTerms: swollen ureter and kidney on ultrasound

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vesicoureteral reflux confirmed by voiding cystourethrogram
Obstruction at the ureterovesical junction causing impaired urine flow
searchTerms: urine flow blocked at bladder exit

common.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass due to hydronephrosis
searchTerms: felt belly lump from kidney swelling

common.symptomName: Poor urinary stream or intermittent urinary flow

occasional.symptomName: Failure to thrive in infants due to recurrent infections
searchTerms: failure to thrive due to UTIs
growth delay in infants with infections
high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues

rare.symptomName: Progressive renal insufficiency or chronic kidney disease
Sepsis secondary to complicated urinary tract infections

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in advanced cases
imaging: Prenatal or postnatal ultrasound demonstrating hydroureteronephrosis
Diuretic renography showing delayed drainage and obstruction at ureterovesical junction
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; primarily sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Urodynamic studies may be used to exclude neurogenic bladder

distinguishingFeatures: Megaureter caused by neurogenic bladder or external compression
Absence of primary distal ureteral obstruction
Obstruction occurs at ureteropelvic junction rather than ureterovesical junction

redFlags: Recurrent febrile urinary tract infections in infancy
Progressive hydronephrosis with declining renal function
Signs of sepsis or systemic infection
references: Orphanet: Congenital primary megaureter, refluxing and obstructed form - ORPHA:544578
